area: Area III. Air Traffic Control (ATC) Clearances and Procedures
objective: By the end of this lesson you can copy a holding clearance, pick and fly the right entry, hold at the right speed with correct timing and wind correction, make the required reports, and redo your fuel plan when ATC gives you a new EFC.
why: Weather, traffic and missed approaches can put you in a hold with little warning. A pilot who can hold calmly, on speed and inside the protected airspace, and who keeps an eye on the fuel clock, has time to think instead of falling behind.

warmup: You are 10 minutes from your clearance limit and ATC says the airport is closed for a disabled airplane on the runway. What do you need to know from ATC, and what do you need to figure out yourself?

key_terms.def: A set maneuver that keeps you inside a specified airspace while you wait for further clearance from ATC.
A fix you can identify by NAVAIDs (or by sight) that anchors the holding pattern.
A holding pattern with right turns.
A holding pattern with left turns. ATC says "left turns" when it wants one.
The side of the holding course on which the pattern is flown. The other side is the nonholding side.
The time you can expect a clearance beyond the clearance limit. Also your leave time if the radios fail.
Highest indicated airspeed allowed in a hold: 200, 230 or 265 KIAS by altitude, unless charted lower.
Lowest altitude for a hold that gives signal coverage, communications and obstacle clearance.
Line through the holding fix, 70° from the holding course on the holding side, that divides the entry sectors.
Advisory that you can accept little or no delay at the destination. Not an emergency.

chunks.title: The holding pattern and its parts

body.p: A hold is a set maneuver that keeps you inside a specified airspace while you wait for further clearance from ATC [[34:357|P/CG H-2]]. The holding fix is a point you can identify by NAVAIDs, or by sight, that anchors the pattern [[34:357|P/CG H-2]].

In no wind, a standard hold looks like a racetrack. You fly the inbound course to the fix, turn 180° to the right, fly a parallel course outbound for 1 minute, turn 180° to the right, and fly the inbound course back to the fix [[23:301|IFH 10-10]].

head: Term
Meaning
rows: Left turns. An ATC clearance always says left turns when a nonstandard pattern is to be flown [[23:301|IFH 10-10]]
The inbound course to the fix. The pattern sits on the holding side of it [[23:301|IFH Figure 10-4]]
The turn at the fix and the turn at the far end of the outbound leg [[33:386|AIM 5-3-8j3(e)]]
The point on the outbound leg even with the fix. Outbound timing starts over or abeam the fix, whichever comes later [[33:387|AIM 5-3-8j4(b)]]

body.p: Why so strict? The protected airspace was built around the FAA's entries, speeds and turns. For level holding, the primary area gives at least 1,000 ft of obstacle clearance [[29:111|IPH 2-51]]. Odd entries, especially with too much speed at the fix, can take you outside the protected airspace [[33:386|AIM 5-3-8j3]].

callout.text: Holding en route is less common today, but published holds are still charted where ATC needs them [[23:29|IFH 1-10]]. You will also hold after missed approaches and fly holds in lieu of a procedure turn [[29:133|IPH 3-21]] [[23:39|IFH 1-20]].

check.q: Which way do you turn in a standard hold, and how long is the first outbound leg at 5,000 ft?

chunks.title: The holding clearance: charted and uncharted

body.p: When ATC clears you to a fix other than the destination and expects a delay, ATC must give complete holding instructions (unless the hold is charted), an EFC time, and its best estimate of any more delay [[33:382|AIM 5-3-8a]]. ATC usually gives a holding clearance at least 5 minutes before you reach the fix [[29:111|IPH 2-51]].

head: Item
Charted (published) hold
Uncharted hold
rows: Direction to hold from the fix
Given, as one of 8 compass points: N, NE, E, SE and so on [[33:382|AIM 5-3-8i]]
Given (may be left out if it is the clearance limit just named) [[33:382|AIM 5-3-8i]]
In miles if DME or RNAV is used; in minutes on request [[33:382|AIM 5-3-8i]]
Said only for left turns, on request, or if the controller thinks it necessary [[33:383|AIM 5-3-8i]]
Given, with any extra delay information [[33:383|AIM 5-3-8i]]

body.p: IPH examples: "Hold southeast of PINNE Intersection as published. Expect further clearance at 1645." and "Hold west of Horst Intersection on Victor 8, 5 mile legs, left turns, expect further clearance at 1430." [[29:110|IPH Figure 2-71]]

Keep your last assigned altitude unless the holding clearance gives a new one, and fly right turns unless left turns are assigned [[29:111|IPH 2-51]]. If the hold is charted and ATC gives no instructions, hold as depicted [[33:382|AIM 5-3-8b]].

No instructions and no charted hold? Ask ATC for holding instructions before you reach the fix [[33:382|AIM 5-3-8c]]. If you still can't get them (busy frequency, stuck mic), enter a standard pattern on the course you flew to the fix and ask for further clearance as soon as you can. ATC protects your altitude at the clearance limit [[33:382|AIM 5-3-8c]].

callout.text: "As published" means ATC may leave out everything except the direction and those words. ATC must always give complete holding instructions if you ask [[33:382|AIM 5-3-8b]].

check.q: You reach your clearance limit with no holding instructions, no charted hold, and a jammed frequency. What do you do?
check.a: Enter a standard (right-turn) pattern on the course you used to reach the fix, at your last assigned altitude, and ask for further clearance as soon as possible [[33:382|AIM 5-3-8c]] [[29:111|IPH 2-51]].

chunks.title: Maximum holding speeds and slowing down

body.p: The size of a hold grows with speed. So maximum holding speeds limit the airspace ATC must protect [[29:112|IPH 2-52]].

bullets: Some holds from 6,001 to 14,000 ft are limited to 210 KIAS. An icon shows it [[33:385|AIM 5-3-8j2(b)]].
Some holds show a speed in parentheses inside the racetrack, like (175). Be at or below it before you first cross the fix [[33:385|AIM 5-3-8j2(b)]].
Can't hold at or below the limit (turbulence, icing)? Tell ATC right away and ask for another clearance [[33:391|AIM 5-3-8j8(a)(2)]].
Fixed-wing airplanes should hold at 90 KIAS or faster to reduce wind drift [[33:390|AIM 5-3-8j8(a)(1)]].

body.p: **When to slow down.** When you are 3 minutes or less from a clearance limit and have no clearance beyond it, start slowing so you cross the fix at or below the maximum holding airspeed [[33:382|AIM 5-3-8d]]. When ATC gives advance notice of holding, be at or below holding speed at least 3 minutes before the fix [[33:390|AIM 5-3-8j8(a)]].

**Fuel.** Slowing down on the way to the fix can shorten the hold or avoid it [[29:112|IPH 2-52]]. Once established, use the holding power and leaning your POH gives, and set it before the fix (ACS IR.III.B.S2).

callout.text: 200, 230, 265: up to 6,000 ft, up to 14,000 ft, above 14,000 ft. Slow down 3 minutes out [[33:385|AIM 5-3-8j2]] [[33:382|AIM 5-3-8d]].

check.q: You will hold at 8,000 ft and the chart shows no speed icon. What is the maximum holding speed?
check.a: 230 KIAS, the limit from 6,001 to 14,000 ft [[33:385|AIM 5-3-8j2(a)]].

chunks.title: Choosing the entry: direct, teardrop or parallel

body.p: The FAA recommends three entries: parallel, teardrop and direct. The holding airspace was sized around them [[33:386|AIM 5-3-8j3(d)]]. Pick the entry from your heading when you arrive at the fix. Within ±5° of a sector line is good enough [[33:391|AIM 5-3-8j8(d)]].

head: Entry
Sector
What you do
rows: (c), the 180° half on the outbound side of the 70° line [[23:303|IFH Figure 10-6]]
Fly to the fix and turn to follow the holding pattern [[33:386|AIM 5-3-8j3(c)]]
(b), the 70° slice behind the fix on the nonholding side [[23:303|IFH Figure 10-6]]

Fly to the fix, turn outbound to a heading 30° off the outbound course into the holding side, fly 1 minute, then turn in the direction of the pattern to intercept the inbound course [[33:386|AIM 5-3-8j3(b)]]
(a), the slice behind the fix on the holding side [[23:303|IFH Figure 10-6]]

Fly to the fix, turn to parallel the holding course outbound on the nonholding side for 1 minute, turn back toward the holding side through more than 180°, and return to the fix or intercept the inbound course [[33:386|AIM 5-3-8j3(a)]] [[33:386|AIM FIG 5-3-4]]

body.p: **Worked example.** "Hold east of the VOR on the 090 radial," right turns. The inbound course is 270°, the outbound course 090°, and the holding side is north. The 70° line runs from the fix toward 020° and 200°. By your heading at the VOR [[23:303|IFH Figure 10-6]]:

bullets: Heading 200° through 270° and 360° to 020°: direct. Cross the VOR and turn right to 090° outbound.
Heading 020° to 090°: teardrop. Cross the VOR, fly about 060° (30° into the holding side) for 1 minute, then turn right to intercept 270° inbound.
Heading 090° to 200°: parallel. Cross the VOR, fly 090° on the south (nonholding) side for 1 minute, then turn left more than 180° to intercept 270° inbound or return to the VOR.

body.p: **Nonstandard (left-turn) holds.** The fix end and outbound end turns are to the left, and the entries are drawn off the 70° line on the holding side the same way, so the whole picture is a mirror image [[33:386|AIM 5-3-8j3(e)]].

callout.text: Many GPS and RNAV systems pick the entry from ground track instead of heading. With a big drift angle you may get an entry you did not expect [[33:388|AIM 5-3-8j7(a)(1)]].

check.q: Hold east of the VOR on the 090 radial, right turns. You arrive at the VOR heading 045°. Which entry, and what heading after the VOR?
check.a: Teardrop: 045° is in the 020° to 090° slice. Fly about 060° for 1 minute, then turn right to intercept 270° inbound [[33:386|AIM 5-3-8j3(b)]] [[23:303|IFH Figure 10-6]].

head: Item
Rule
rows: 1 minute at or below 14,000 ft MSL; 1½ minutes above 14,000 ft [[33:387|AIM 5-3-8j4(a)]]
1 minute (1½ above 14,000). After that, adjust outbound timing to get the right inbound time [[33:387|AIM 5-3-8j4 NOTE]]
Over or abeam the fix, whichever is later. Can't tell abeam? Start when the turn to outbound is complete [[33:387|AIM 5-3-8j4(b)]]
Start the turn outbound at the first complete reversal of the TO/FROM indicator [[33:382|AIM 5-3-8g]]
3° per second, or 30° bank, or 25° bank with a flight director, whichever needs the least bank [[33:391|AIM 5-3-8j8(b)]]
Your first time of arrival over the fix [[23:303|IFH 10-12]]

body.p: **DME and GPS holds.** Same entries and procedures, but you use distances instead of time. ATC or the chart gives the outbound leg length, and the DME or GPS along-track distance (ATD) shows where it ends [[33:387|AIM 5-3-8j5]]. Inbound toward the NAVAID with the fix at 10 DME and 5 NM legs, the outbound leg ends at 15 DME. Inbound away from the NAVAID with the fix at 28 DME and 8 NM legs, it ends at 20 DME [[33:387|AIM 5-3-8j5]].

**Restrictions.** For a hold in lieu of a procedure turn, fly the direction as depicted, don't exceed the charted leg length or time, and stay within the maximum holding speeds [[33:428|AIM 5-4-9]]. If you are cleared for the approach before you get back to the fix and you are at the right altitude, extra circuits are not needed or expected [[23:39|IFH 1-20]].

callout.text: In a light airplane, a standard-rate turn needs well under 30° of bank. Only above about 210 KTAS does standard rate need more than 30° [[29:112|IPH 2-52]].

check.q: You hold at an airway intersection and can't tell when you are abeam the fix. When do you start the outbound timing?
check.a: When the turn to outbound is complete [[33:387|AIM 5-3-8j4(b)]] [[23:303|IFH Figure 10-7]].

chunks.title: Wind correction and leaving on time

body.p: With wind you can't fly a neat, symmetrical racetrack. Correct for a known wind except while turning, and adjust outbound timing to get a 1-minute inbound leg (1½ above 14,000 ft) [[23:301|IFH 10-10]].

bullets: Correct for wind mainly with drift correction on the inbound and outbound legs [[33:391|AIM 5-3-8j8(c)]].
Outbound, triple the inbound drift correction. Correcting 8° left inbound means 24° right outbound [[33:391|AIM 5-3-8j8(c)]].
Time each inbound leg. If it was longer than 1 minute, shorten the next outbound leg; if it was shorter, lengthen it [[33:387|AIM 5-3-8j4 NOTE]].
DME, GPS or any other navigation you have may be used to check the inbound leg time [[33:387|AIM 5-3-8j4 NOTE]].

body.p: **Worked example.** Inbound course 270°. To track it you need a heading of 275° (5° right, so the wind is from the north). Outbound on 090° the wind is now on your left, so correct left three times as much: 090° - 15° = 075° [[33:391|AIM 5-3-8j8(c)]].

**Leaving on time.** If ATC gives you a time to leave the fix, adjust your path inside the pattern so you leave at that exact time [[33:391|AIM 5-3-8k]]. Plan the last lap of the hold to leave the fix as close as possible to the EFC [[29:111|IPH 2-51]]. After you leave, go back to normal speed within any other speed rules [[33:391|AIM 5-3-8k]].

callout.text: Wind: correct on the legs, not in the turns. Triple it outbound. Fix the inbound time by changing the outbound time [[23:301|IFH 10-10]] [[33:391|AIM 5-3-8j8(c)]].

check.q: Inbound you hold 4° left of the course to track it. What wind correction do you use outbound?
check.a: About 12° right: three times the inbound correction, the other way [[33:391|AIM 5-3-8j8(c)]].

body.p: Report the time and altitude when you reach the clearance limit, and report leaving it [[33:382|AIM 5-3-8f]]. Both reports are made without an ATC request [[33:377|AIM 5-3-3]].

head: Report
IPH example
rows: Time and altitude on reaching a holding fix
Tell ATC right away and ask for another clearance [[33:391|AIM 5-3-8j8(a)(2)]]

body.p: ATC also issues new instructions when the delay will exceed 1 hour, when a revised EFC is needed, and when you report the weather is below your minimums [[23:302|IFH 10-11]]. When no delay is expected, the controller should clear you beyond the fix at least 5 minutes before you get there [[33:382|AIM 5-3-8e]].

Leave the holding fix when ATC clears you on or for the approach, as 14 CFR part 91 allows (for example after two-way radio failure), or after you cancel IFR while holding in VFR conditions [[23:304|IFH 10-13]]. ATC must know when you leave before it can clear the next airplane into your airspace [[23:304|IFH 10-13]].

callout.text: Radio failure in IFR conditions while holding (14 CFR 91.185): if the holding fix is where an approach begins, start the descent and approach as close as possible to the EFC. If not, leave the fix at the EFC, go to a fix where an approach begins, and start the approach as close as possible to your ETA [[60:483|14 CFR 91.185(c)(3)]].

check.q: Which two holding reports does the AIM expect without being asked?
check.a: Time and altitude on reaching the holding fix, and when leaving it [[33:377|AIM 5-3-3]].

chunks.title: Holding with GPS, RNAV and the MFD

body.p: GPS and other RNAV systems can steer you through a hold, but each one does it a little differently. You are expected to know how yours works [[33:388|AIM 5-3-8j7]]. All holds are still designed with the conventional criteria, so small RNAV differences can add up to take you outside the protected airspace [[33:388|AIM 5-3-8j7(a)]].

bullets: Entry may be picked from ground track, not heading [[33:388|AIM 5-3-8j7(a)(1)]].
The design assumes you fly over the fix on entry. A GPS fly-by turn there, especially in a direct entry from the holding side, can take you outside protected airspace [[33:388|AIM 5-3-8j7(a)(2)]].
Many systems treat leg length as the maximum inbound leg, so the outbound turn point can move past the design point. A strong headwind outbound makes it worse [[33:389|AIM 5-3-8j7(a)(4)]].

A database may keep only one hold per fix. Check that turn direction, speed limit, timing and distance match the hold you were given. For an uncharted hold, you program the course, turns, speed and leg [[33:390|AIM 5-3-8j7(c)]].
Changes made close to the fix may not take effect until the next circuit [[33:390|AIM 5-3-8j7(c)(3)]].

body.p: A moving map on a multi-function display (MFD) shows where you are in relation to NAVAIDs, waypoints, airspace and terrain, which builds situational awareness [[23:29|IFH 1-10]]. An HSI also lowers workload for a holding entry by showing heading and course together [[23:254|IFH 9-11]]. Use both to check that what the airplane is doing matches the hold in your head.

Learn your GPS: entering, flying and exiting holds, and flying a route from a hold, are on the FAA's list of receiver skills to master [[23:275|IFH 9-32]]. Some receivers need you to stop waypoint sequencing by hand in a hold and resume it after [[23:273|IFH 9-30]].

callout.text: Be ready to take over if the GPS does not start the inbound turn within a reasonable distance of the charted leg length, especially in a hold in lieu of a procedure turn. Tell ATC if the outbound leg gets too long [[33:391|AIM 5-3-8j8(f)]].

check.q: Your GPS has a hold stored at the fix, but ATC assigned left turns. What do you do?
check.a: Check and change the hold in the GPS. You must confirm the turn direction, speed limit, timing and distance match the hold you were given [[33:390|AIM 5-3-8j7(c)(1)]].

chunks.title: Fly it step by step: from clearance to leaving

bullets: 1. Copy the clearance: direction, fix, course, leg length, turns, EFC [[33:382|AIM 5-3-8i]]. If anything is unclear, ask; "roger" only means ATC heard you [[29:111|IPH 2-51]].
2. Picture the hold on the chart, HSI or MFD. Pick the entry from the heading you expect at the fix [[33:391|AIM 5-3-8j8(d)]].
3. Note the EFC and work out your fuel (see the risk chunk) [[29:112|IPH 2-52]].
4. 3 minutes or less from the fix, slow to holding speed and set holding power [[33:382|AIM 5-3-8d]].
5. Recognize the fix (TO/FROM flip, DME or GPS) and start the entry turn right away. Note the time and report time and altitude [[33:382|AIM 5-3-8f]] [[33:382|AIM 5-3-8g]].
6. Fly the entry with turns at standard rate or 30° bank, whichever is less [[33:391|AIM 5-3-8j8(b)]].
7. Outbound: start timing over or abeam the fix, whichever is later, and triple the inbound drift correction [[33:387|AIM 5-3-8j4(b)]] [[33:391|AIM 5-3-8j8(c)]].
8. Inbound: time the leg and adjust the next outbound leg [[33:387|AIM 5-3-8j4 NOTE]].
9. Plan the last lap to leave at the EFC or the time ATC gives, and report leaving [[33:391|AIM 5-3-8k]] [[33:382|AIM 5-3-8f]].

callout.text: SRM in the hold: use every resource, inside and outside the airplane. ATC, the GPS and MFD, and checklists all help, but in a busy moment you must prioritize tasks and manage workload [[30:56|RMH 8-3]]. Fly the airplane first; program the box second.

check.q: When does the ACS want you to slow to holding speed?
check.a: When 3 minutes or less from, but before reaching, the holding fix (ACS IR.III.B.S2), which matches the AIM [[33:382|AIM 5-3-8d]].

chunks.title: Risk: EFC, fuel, weather and emergencies

body.p: **Why holds happen.** Controllers assign holds for deteriorating weather, heavy traffic, and after missed approaches [[29:133|IPH 3-21]]. "Delay indefinite" with an EFC is used when ATC can't yet estimate the delay, for example a disabled aircraft on the runway, saturated airspace, or weather below landing minimums [[34:335|P/CG D-2]].
If the reported weather drops below your minimums while you hold, tell ATC. ATC then gives instructions to keep holding for better weather or to go to another airport [[23:302|IFH 10-11]].

**Every new EFC means new fuel math.** Your yardstick is the IFR fuel rule: fuel to the first airport of intended landing, then to the alternate (if one is required), then 45 minutes at normal cruise [[60:468|14 CFR 91.167]] [[60:469|14 CFR 91.167(a)(3)]]. Keep a time and fuel record and compare actual burn to planned [[29:112|IPH 2-52]].

bullets: **Minimum fuel**: say it when, on reaching the destination, you can't accept any undue delay. It is not an emergency and does not get you priority [[34:10|AIM 5-5-15]].

**Emergency**: if your fuel means you need priority to land safely, declare an emergency for low fuel and report fuel remaining in minutes [[34:10|AIM 5-5-15]]. That time includes reserve fuel and an allowance for gauge error [[34:349|P/CG F-6]].
You are in at least an urgency condition the moment you are doubtful about fuel endurance or weather. Ask for help then, not later [[34:28|AIM 6-1-2]].
In an emergency, the PIC may deviate from any rule of part 91 to the extent needed [[60:435|14 CFR 91.3]].

callout.text: Know your diversion airports before you need them. A single pilot who has the frequencies and approaches for nearby airports ready can divert with crew-like efficiency [[30:57|RMH 8-4]].

check.q: What is the difference between "minimum fuel" and a fuel emergency?
check.a: Minimum fuel says you can accept little or no delay but gets no priority. If you need priority to land safely, declare an emergency and give fuel remaining in minutes [[34:10|AIM 5-5-15]].

bullets: Crossing the fix too fast. Excess speed plus an odd entry can take you outside the protected airspace [[33:386|AIM 5-3-8j3]].
Picking the entry from a guess about position instead of your heading at the fix [[33:391|AIM 5-3-8j8(d)]].
In a parallel entry, turning away from the holding side after the 1-minute leg [[33:386|AIM FIG 5-3-4]].
Starting outbound timing at the fix instead of over or abeam it, whichever is later [[33:387|AIM 5-3-8j4(b)]].
Correcting for wind in the turns, or using the same correction outbound as inbound instead of three times as much [[23:301|IFH 10-10]] [[33:391|AIM 5-3-8j8(c)]].
Flying 1 minute outbound every time instead of adjusting it to get a 1-minute inbound leg [[33:387|AIM 5-3-8j4 NOTE]].
Forgetting the reports: time and altitude at the fix, and leaving it [[33:382|AIM 5-3-8f]].
Trusting a stored GPS hold without checking turn direction and leg length [[33:390|AIM 5-3-8j7(c)(1)]].
Using an autopilot bank limit under 25°, which widens and lengthens the pattern [[33:389|AIM 5-3-8j7(a)(3)]].

check.q: Your inbound legs keep coming out at 1 minute 20 seconds. What should you change?
check.a: Shorten the next outbound leg to bring the inbound leg back to 1 minute [[33:387|AIM 5-3-8j4 NOTE]].

scenario.title: Holding for weather with the fuel clock running
scenario.setup: You are IFR at 5,000 ft in your training airplane, flying direct to the ABC VOR on a heading of 225°. The weather at your destination is dropping toward minimums. At 1450 approach says: "Hold west of the ABC VOR on the 270 radial, maintain 5,000, expect further clearance 1530." Wind is from the north at 20 knots. You have 32 gallons and plan 10 GPH for every phase. After the hold, the approach and landing take 15 minutes, and your alternate is 30 minutes from the destination.

questions.q: What entry do you fly at the VOR, and what heading after you cross it?
questions.a: The inbound course is 090° with right turns, so the holding side is south. Arriving on 225° puts you in the teardrop slice (200° to 270° for this hold). Fly about 240° (outbound 270° minus 30° into the holding side) for 1 minute, then turn right to intercept 090° inbound [[33:386|AIM 5-3-8j3(b)]] [[23:303|IFH Figure 10-6]].

questions.q: When do you slow down, and what do you tell ATC at the VOR?
questions.a: Be at holding speed when 3 minutes or less from the VOR [[33:382|AIM 5-3-8d]]. At the VOR, report the time and altitude, for example "ABC VOR at 57, 5,000, holding west" [[33:382|AIM 5-3-8f]] [[29:105|IPH 2-45]].

questions.q: Inbound on 090° you need a heading of 084° to track. What heading do you fly outbound?
questions.a: Triple the 6° left correction and apply it to the right: 270° + 18° = 288°. Then adjust the outbound time to get 1-minute inbound legs [[33:391|AIM 5-3-8j8(c)]] [[23:301|IFH 10-10]].

questions.q: At 1510 ATC revises your EFC to 1630. You now have about 28.7 gallons. Can you wait?
questions.a: Holding 80 more minutes, plus 15 for the approach, 30 to the alternate and 45 in reserve, is 170 minutes, about 28.3 gallons. 28.7 gallons is about 172 minutes, so you would have only about 2 minutes of margin [[60:468|14 CFR 91.167]] [[60:469|14 CFR 91.167(a)(3)]]. Tell ATC now and ask for your alternate, or a closer airport with better weather [[23:302|IFH 10-11]].

questions.q: On the way to the alternate ATC starts vectoring you for spacing. When do you say "minimum fuel," and when do you declare an emergency?
questions.a: Say "minimum fuel" once you can't accept any undue delay on arrival; it gets no priority. If you need priority to land safely, declare an emergency and give fuel remaining in minutes [[34:10|AIM 5-5-15]]. Once you doubt your fuel endurance, you are already in an urgency condition [[34:28|AIM 6-1-2]].

questions.q: What SRM resources help you most in this hold?
questions.a: ATC (weather at other airports, a direct route, priority if needed), the GPS and MFD to keep the hold and nearest airports in view, and your fuel and time log. Prioritize: fly the hold first, then plan [[30:56|RMH 8-3]] [[23:29|IFH 1-10]] [[29:112|IPH 2-52]].

skills.do: Choose and fly the right entry (direct, teardrop or parallel) for a standard, nonstandard, published or non-published hold.
skills.practice: Before each practice hold, say the inbound course, the holding side and the entry for your expected heading at the fix [[33:391|AIM 5-3-8j8(d)]]. Sketch the 70° line on the chart or picture it on the HSI [[23:303|IFH Figure 10-6]].

skills.do: Slow to holding speed when 3 minutes or less from, but before, the holding fix, and set power for fuel conservation.
skills.practice: Time 3 minutes from the fix and slow then, as in the IFH racetrack drill [[23:191|IFH 7-30]] [[33:382|AIM 5-3-8d]]. Use the holding power and leaning from your POH.

skills.do: Recognize arrival at the holding fix and start the entry promptly.
skills.practice: Call out fix passage (TO/FROM flip, DME, GPS) and begin the turn without delay [[33:382|AIM 5-3-8g]].

skills.do: Comply with the hold's leg length and other restrictions, such as published speed limits and hold in lieu of procedure turn limits.
skills.practice: Fly DME holds where the outbound leg ends at a set distance [[33:387|AIM 5-3-8j5]]. Fly a hold in lieu of a procedure turn without exceeding the charted leg [[33:428|AIM 5-4-9]].

skills.do: Hold airspeed ±10 knots, altitude ±100 ft, headings ±10°, and course within ¾-scale CDI deflection (ACS IR.III.B.S4).
skills.practice: Trim for holding speed before the fix. Fly the IFH racetrack pattern by the clock to build the scan [[23:191|IFH 7-30]].

skills.do: Correct for wind to keep the pattern and arrive over the fix as close as possible to a specified time.
skills.practice: Triple the inbound drift correction outbound and adjust outbound time for 1-minute inbound legs [[33:391|AIM 5-3-8j8(c)]]. Have your instructor give you a time to leave the fix [[33:391|AIM 5-3-8k]].

skills.do: Use the MFD and other moving-map displays, if installed, to monitor your position in the hold.
skills.practice: Load and fly holds in your GPS, then check the map against your heading and timing [[23:275|IFH 9-32]]. Practice catching a wrong turn direction or leg in the box [[33:390|AIM 5-3-8j7(c)(1)]].

skills.do: Make the holding reports and follow ATC restrictions.
skills.practice: Say the reports out loud on every practice hold: time and altitude at the fix, and leaving [[29:105|IPH 2-45]].

skills.do: Use SRM: manage workload, automation and ATC while holding.
skills.practice: Practice holds with a new EFC thrown in, and redo the fuel plan while flying the hold [[30:56|RMH 8-3]] [[29:112|IPH 2-52]].

quiz.q: You are told to hold at 5,000 ft MSL with no speed shown on the chart. What is the maximum holding airspeed?
quiz.why: From the MHA to 6,000 ft the limit is 200 KIAS. 230 KIAS is for 6,001 to 14,000 ft [[33:385|AIM 5-3-8j2(a)]].

quiz.q: In an uncharted holding clearance, when does ATC state the direction of turns?
options: For left turns, on pilot request, or when the controller thinks it necessary
Only when DME is used for the legs
quiz.why: Turn direction is given if left turns are to be made, the pilot asks, or the controller thinks it necessary [[33:383|AIM 5-3-8i]].

quiz.q: Hold east of the VOR on the 090 radial, right turns. You arrive at the VOR heading 150°. Which entry?
options: Any entry, since none is required
quiz.why: For this hold the parallel slice is headings 090° to 200° [[23:303|IFH Figure 10-6]]. The FAA recommends the three standard entries [[33:386|AIM 5-3-8j3(d)]].

quiz.q: When do you start timing the outbound leg?
options: Over or abeam the fix, whichever occurs later
The moment you cross the fix
When you roll out of the inbound turn
One minute after crossing the fix
quiz.why: Outbound timing starts over or abeam the fix, whichever is later; if abeam can't be found, when the outbound turn is complete [[33:387|AIM 5-3-8j4(b)]].

quiz.q: Inbound you correct 3° right for wind. What correction do you use outbound?
quiz.why: Triple the inbound correction and apply it the other way: 9° left [[33:391|AIM 5-3-8j8(c)]].

quiz.q: Holding at a VOR, when do you begin the turn to the outbound leg?
options: At the first complete reversal of the TO/FROM indicator
30 seconds after the needle starts to move
quiz.why: At a VOR, begin the outbound turn at the first complete reversal of the TO/FROM indicator [[33:382|AIM 5-3-8g]].

quiz.q: What do you report to ATC on reaching the holding fix?
quiz.why: Report the time and altitude on reaching the clearance limit, and report leaving it [[33:382|AIM 5-3-8f]].

quiz.q: A "minimum fuel" advisory tells ATC that:
options: You can accept no undue delay, but it is not an emergency
You need priority handling to land
You have less than 45 minutes of fuel
quiz.why: Minimum fuel means you can't accept any undue delay at the destination. It is not an emergency and does not mean priority [[34:10|AIM 5-5-15]].

quiz.q: Without a flight director or RNAV guidance, what bank do you use for holding turns?
options: Always 45° to stay close to the fix
3° per second or 30°, whichever needs less bank
quiz.why: Use 3° per second or 30° bank (25° with a flight director), whichever requires the least bank [[33:391|AIM 5-3-8j8(b)]].

quiz.q: Why might a GPS give you an unexpected holding entry in a strong crosswind?
options: It picks the entry from ground track, not heading
It always flies a direct entry
It uses 1½-minute legs at all altitudes
quiz.why: Many systems use ground track angle instead of heading, so a big drift angle can change the entry [[33:388|AIM 5-3-8j7(a)(1)]].

takeaways: Charted hold: direction, fix and EFC. Uncharted: add the course, leg length and left turns if used.
Max holding speeds: 200 KIAS to 6,000 ft, 230 to 14,000, 265 above. Slow down 3 minutes out.
Pick the entry from your heading at the fix: direct, teardrop (30° into the holding side) or parallel (1 minute, then turn back more than 180°).
1-minute inbound legs (1½ above 14,000). Time outbound from over or abeam the fix, whichever is later, and adjust it.
Wind: correct on the legs, and triple the inbound correction outbound.
Report time and altitude at the fix and when leaving. With lost comms, the EFC is your leave time.
Every new EFC means new fuel math. Minimum fuel is not an emergency; declare one when you need priority.
cfi_notes: The IFH (10-12) tells readers to review "paragraph 5-3-7 in the AIM" for entries. In the current AIM, holding is paragraph 5-3-8 [[23:303|IFH 10-12]] [[33:382|AIM 5-3-8]].

The IFH uses "MHA" for maximum holding airspeed [[23:302|IFH 10-11]], but the P/CG and the AIM speed table use MHA for minimum holding altitude [[34:379|P/CG M-4]] [[33:385|AIM 5-3-8j2]]. Teach the current meaning.

The IFH speed table says "up to 6,000 feet" and lists "a bank angle provided by a flight director system." The current AIM says MHA to 6,000 ft and 25° with a flight director, using whichever bank is least [[33:385|AIM 5-3-8j2]] [[33:391|AIM 5-3-8j8(b)]].

The AIM text says the parallel entry turns "in the direction of the holding pattern" through more than 180°. Students read that as a right turn in a standard hold. Use FIG 5-3-4 and IFH Figure 10-6 to show the return turn goes back toward the holding side [[33:386|AIM FIG 5-3-4]].

The heading arcs in the worked example (direct, teardrop, parallel) are drawn from the 70° line in IFH Figure 10-6. Have students build them for several holds on paper before flying, then check with the HSI.
Examiners often probe: entry choice, slowing 3 minutes out, the two reports, how the EFC is used with lost comms, and fuel after an EFC change [[60:483|14 CFR 91.185(c)(3)]].
Common student error: timing the outbound leg from fix passage on a VOR hold instead of from abeam or TO/FROM reversal. Use IFH Figure 10-7 [[23:303|IFH Figure 10-7]].
IPH 2-51 says an uncharted hold at Cherrelyn would be flown west on V214 with right turns, the course the airplane arrived on. Use it to drill the no-instructions rule [[29:111|IPH 2-51]].
gaps: No uploaded handbook has a common-errors list for holding; the common errors chunk is built from AIM 5-3-8 cautions and IFH figures.
Holding power settings, fuel flows and leaning for the training airplane come from its POH/AFM, which is not in the sources.
The sources give no rule of thumb for how many seconds to change the outbound leg per second of inbound error; students learn it by practice.
Holding pages and buttons differ by GPS and MFD model; use the manufacturer's pilot guide for the installed unit.
The "6 Ts" (or 5 Ts) memory aid is not in the uploaded FAA sources, so the order game uses the AIM parallel entry instead.

activities.title: Take apart a holding clearance
activities.intro: Tap a piece of the clearance, then what it tells you.

pairs.r: Direction of the hold from the fix
Outbound leg length by DME or GPS
Time you can expect clearance beyond the fix

activities.title: Pick the entry: hold east on the 090 radial, right turns
activities.intro: Tap a clue, then tap where it belongs.

activities.title: Fly a parallel entry
activities.intro: Use the arrows to put the steps in order, then tap Check.
steps: Slow to holding speed when 3 minutes or less from the fix
Cross the fix and note the time
Turn to parallel the holding course outbound on the nonholding side
Turn back toward the holding side through more than 180°
Intercept the inbound course or return to the fix
At the fix, turn outbound to follow the pattern

activities.title: True or false: holding rules
activities.intro: Decide if each statement is true or false.

cards.s: Holding at 9,000 ft with no speed limit charted, you may fly up to 230 KIAS.
cards.why: Yes. 6,001 to 14,000 ft allows 230 KIAS unless a lower limit is charted [[33:385|AIM 5-3-8j2(a)]].

cards.s: Above 14,000 ft MSL, the inbound leg is 1 minute.
cards.why: No. Above 14,000 ft MSL it is 1½ minutes [[33:387|AIM 5-3-8j4(a)]].

cards.s: If you correct 6° left inbound, you correct about 18° right outbound.
cards.why: Yes. Triple the inbound drift correction outbound, the other way [[33:391|AIM 5-3-8j8(c)]].

cards.s: If a charted hold is at your clearance limit and ATC gives no holding instructions, you hold as depicted.
cards.why: Yes. You are expected to hold as depicted on the chart [[33:382|AIM 5-3-8b]].

cards.s: Saying "minimum fuel" gets you priority over other traffic.
cards.why: No. A minimum fuel advisory does not imply a need for traffic priority. Declare an emergency if you need priority [[34:10|AIM 5-5-15]].

cards.s: With two-way radio failure, holding at a fix where your approach begins, you start the approach as close as possible to the EFC.
cards.why: Yes. Begin descent or descent and approach as close as possible to the EFC time [[60:483|14 CFR 91.185(c)(3)]].

cards.s: You must fly the first outbound leg for 1 minute on every circuit, no matter what the inbound leg time is.
cards.why: No. Only the first outbound leg is 1 minute; later outbound legs are adjusted to get the right inbound time [[33:387|AIM 5-3-8j4 NOTE]].

final_quiz.q: "Hold south of the ABC VOR on the 180 radial," no turn direction given. You arrive at the VOR heading 135°. What do you fly?
final_quiz.why: No turns stated means right turns, so the inbound course is 360° and the holding side is east [[29:111|IPH 2-51]]. 135° falls in the teardrop slice (110° to 180°) [[23:303|IFH Figure 10-6]]. The teardrop heading is 30° off the 180° outbound course into the holding side: 150° [[33:386|AIM 5-3-8j3(b)]].

final_quiz.q: "Hold west of the 12 DME fix on the 270 radial, 4 mile legs." At what DME does the outbound leg end?
final_quiz.why: Holding west of a fix west of the station puts the inbound leg toward the NAVAID, so the outbound end is farther out: 12 + 4 = 16 DME [[33:387|AIM 5-3-8j5]].

final_quiz.q: "Hold northeast of the 25 DME fix on the 225 radial, 6 mile legs." At what DME does the outbound leg end?
final_quiz.why: The pattern lies between the fix and the station, so the inbound leg is away from the NAVAID and the outbound end is closer in: 25 - 6 = 19 DME [[33:387|AIM 5-3-8j5]].

final_quiz.q: Your groundspeed is 150 knots toward a clearance limit with no clearance beyond it. About how far out must you start slowing at the latest?
final_quiz.why: Start slowing when 3 minutes or less from the fix [[33:382|AIM 5-3-8d]]. 150 knots is 2.5 NM per minute, so 3 minutes is 7.5 NM.

final_quiz.q: Inbound course 090°. You need a heading of 082° to track it. What outbound heading do you fly?
final_quiz.why: Inbound you correct 8° left, so outbound correct 24° right: 270° + 24° = 294° [[33:391|AIM 5-3-8j8(c)]]. 246° applies the correction the wrong way.

final_quiz.q: Holding at 6,000 ft, your inbound legs keep taking 45 seconds. What do you change?
options: Use a 45° bank in the turns
final_quiz.why: Adjust outbound timing to get a 1-minute inbound leg; a short inbound leg means a longer outbound leg [[33:387|AIM 5-3-8j4 NOTE]] [[23:301|IFH 10-10]].

final_quiz.q: You have 24 gallons and burn 8 GPH. After the hold you need 15 minutes for the approach, 30 to the alternate, and the 45-minute reserve. How long can you hold?
final_quiz.why: 15 + 30 + 45 = 90 minutes, or 12 gallons. That leaves 12 gallons, or 1.5 hours of holding [[60:468|14 CFR 91.167]] [[60:469|14 CFR 91.167(a)(3)]]. 135 minutes forgets the 45-minute reserve.

final_quiz.q: In IMC your radios fail while you hold at an en route fix that is not where an approach begins. Your EFC is 1520. What do you do?
options: Leave right away and fly to the destination
Leave at 1520, go to an approach fix, and start the approach close to your ETA
Hold until you are low on fuel, then land
Leave at 1520 and start a descent to the MDA
final_quiz.why: If the clearance limit is not where an approach begins, leave at the EFC, proceed to a fix where an approach begins, and start the approach as close as possible to the ETA [[60:483|14 CFR 91.185(c)(3)]].

final_quiz.q: Holding for weather, your fuel is now so low that you need to land ahead of other traffic. What should you say?
options: Request a lower altitude to save fuel
Declare an emergency for low fuel and give fuel remaining in minutes
final_quiz.why: If you need traffic priority to land safely, declare an emergency due to low fuel and report fuel remaining in minutes. Minimum fuel does not get priority [[34:10|AIM 5-5-15]].

final_quiz.q: ATC says "hold as published," and the chart shows (175) inside the racetrack. What must you do?
options: Be at or below 175 KIAS before you first cross the fix
Slow to 175 KIAS after the entry is complete
Ignore it below 6,000 ft, where 200 KIAS applies
final_quiz.why: A speed in parentheses is a maximum for that hold. Be at or below it before first crossing the fix to stay in the protected airspace [[33:385|AIM 5-3-8j2(b)]].

final_quiz.q: On a direct entry from the holding side, why does the AIM caution against letting the GPS fly a fly-by turn at the fix?
options: The protected airspace assumes you fly over the fix, so a fly-by can take you outside it
It makes the inbound leg exactly 1 minute
It cancels the EFC in the GPS
final_quiz.why: Holding protection assumes fly-over at entry. A fly-by turn on a direct entry from the holding side may take you beyond protected airspace [[33:388|AIM 5-3-8j7(a)(2)]].

final_quiz.q: While you hold, the destination weather drops below your approach minimums. What is the right move?
options: Keep quiet and wait for the EFC
Fly the approach anyway and look for the runway
Tell ATC; it will let you keep holding for better weather or send you elsewhere
final_quiz.why: When you advise ATC that weather is below your minimums, ATC issues instructions to continue holding or proceed to another airport [[23:302|IFH 10-11]].

final_quiz.q: Eastbound on V214, the VORTAC is your clearance limit. No hold is charted, no instructions came, and you can't reach ATC. How do you hold?
options: West of the VORTAC on V214, right turns
East of the VORTAC, left turns
Any direction, as long as you stay at the MEA
Circle over the VORTAC until ATC calls
final_quiz.why: Hold on the inbound course you arrived on, using right turns. Arriving eastbound on V214, that means west of the VORTAC on V214 [[29:111|IPH 2-51]] [[33:382|AIM 5-3-8c]].
